conventions.testing: Unit tests in mod tests blocks within each language file; integration tests via SemanticExtractor::extract_def_use_for_file
conventions.linting: clippy with -D warnings; clippy.toml configured; rustfmt via rust-toolchain.toml
conventions.error_handling: Result types with thiserror; Option for nullable values; expect/unwrap denied by clippy

patterns: Language registration via get_language_info() and get_ts_language() match arms
Query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) defined as pub const &str in language module
Handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance) as pub fn in language module
Extension registration in EXTENSION_MAP in lang.rs
Tree-sitter grammar added to [workspace.dependencies] and unconditional dependency in aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml

related_issues.title: feat(lang): add Swift grammar support
related_issues.relevance: Primary issue defining requirements for Swift support

constraints: DEFUSE_QUERY is mandatory - LanguageInfo.defuse_query field must be populated for all languages
No feature flags - all languages unconditionally compiled in
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 has tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 as only normal dependency (tree-sitter is dev-only)
test_coverage: Existing language files (java.rs, kotlin.rs, etc.) have unit tests for extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance, ELEMENT_QUERY validation, and defuse_query write sites. Swift will follow same pattern.

library_findings.notes: Normal dependency is tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 only; tree-sitter is dev-only. Grammar uses class_declaration with declaration_kind field for class/struct/actor/enum/extension. Separate protocol_declaration node. inheritance_specifier with inherits_from field for type inheritance.
Workspace version; tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 compatible via tree-sitter-language abstraction

approaches.name: Follow Java pattern exactly
approaches.description: Create swift.rs mirroring java.rs structure: ELEMENT_QUERY for function_declaration/class_declaration/protocol_declaration, DEFUSE_QUERY for local_variable_declaration/assignment_expression/identifier, extract_inheritance walking inheritance_specifier->inherits_from->type_identifier. Wire up in mod.rs and lang.rs following css pattern.
cons: Swift has no separate struct/enum/extension declarations (all class_declaration)
Swift inheritance syntax differs from Java (no extends/implements keywords)

approaches.name: Leverage tags.scm queries
approaches.description: Adapt existing tree-sitter-swift tags.scm patterns for ELEMENT_QUERY. Use highlights.scm for CALL_QUERY and REFERENCE_QUERY.
cons: May need adaptation for aptu-coder's capture naming conventions
tags.scm has nested patterns requiring flattening

approaches.name: Minimal viable implementation
approaches.description: Implement only ELEMENT_QUERY (function/class/protocol) and DEFUSE_QUERY. Skip extract_inheritance and receiver handlers initially.
cons: May need rework when inheritance support added

recommendation: Approach 1 (Follow Java pattern exactly) is recommended because it maintains consistency with the codebase, provides complete feature coverage as specified in the issue, and has a clear test strategy. The minor differences between Swift and Java (declaration_kind field, inheritance syntax) are well-documented in the issue and grammar inspection.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-swift grammar (alex-pinkus/tree-sitter-swift): Walk class_declaration's _inheritance_specifiers children. For each inheritance_specifier node, read the inherits_from field which points to a user_type node. Extract the type_identifier text from within user_type to get the base type name. Multiple inheritance_specifiers are siblings (comma-separated in source), so iterate all of them. No distinction between superclass and protocols in the AST - both appear as inheritance_specifier nodes.
